character rules: African American adults with varied skin tones and contemporary features; natural curls, locs, braids, twists, afros, silk presses, and protective styles may appear across the collection. Avoid repeating one hairstyle.
scene rules: Homes, porches, neighborhood parks, community rooms, gardens, libraries, kitchens, and family spaces that feel recognizably lived in. Favor ordinary moments of dignity, connection, and progress.
line style: Crisp black line art with expressive faces and hands, clear silhouettes, moderate interior detail, and broad colorable areas.
detail level: Moderate detail; intimate pages may use richer hair/textile detail while keeping backgrounds simple.
quote page style: Centered affirmations with optional botanical, textile, or geometric framing. Keep typography subordinate to the illustration.
seasonal cues: Spring growth and rain; summer porch/garden light; fall grounding and textured textiles; winter lamps, quilts, and warm interiors.
forbidden: Stereotypes, costume-like cultural props, trauma imagery, violence, drug use, visible injury, police scenes, weapons, restraints, or despair-centered compositions.
notes: The line should feel contemporary, warm, dignified, and distinctly Black American without implying one single Black experience.

character rules: Hispanic American adults with varied skin tones, facial structures, hair textures, curls, waves, straight styles, braids, and contemporary everyday hairstyles. Vary ages, body types, and presentation.
scene rules: Use lived-in apartments, kitchens, patios, courtyards, gardens, community centers, neighborhood walks, family tables, and quiet personal spaces. Small details such as handmade ceramics, woven textiles, potted herbs, family photos, or simple tile can appear selectively.
line style: Crisp black line art with graceful facial expressions, readable hands, natural anatomy, and enough open space for adult coloring.
detail level: Moderate detail with culturally meaningful micro-details used selectively rather than decorating every surface.
quote page style: Use English or bilingual affirmations only when the specific page calls for them. Keep text clear, short, and secondary to the composition.
seasonal cues: Spring blossoms and rain; summer sunlight, garden produce, patios, and water; fall textiles, tea, leaves, and gathering spaces; winter quilts, candles, warm drinks, and family interiors.
forbidden: Pan-Latin stereotypes, costume-like clothing, forced flags or national symbols, exaggerated features, trauma imagery, violence, drug use, visible injury, police scenes, weapons, or crisis-centered scenes.
notes: Hispanic identity should be visible through believable people, relationships, homes, and selective cultural details—not a checklist of clichés. Do not assume one nationality.

character rules: Multiracial adults with visibly varied complexions, hair textures, facial features, and contemporary styles; representation should include different combinations rather than one repeated look.
scene rules: Blended families, mixed-background friendships, apartments, parks, community rooms, kitchens, porches, and personal retreats. Make belonging and everyday connection visually central.
line style: Crisp black line art with clear figure silhouettes, natural anatomy, expressive but calm faces, and broad open coloring spaces.
detail level: Moderate detail with varied hair, textile, and environmental textures while avoiding dense backgrounds.
quote page style: Centered affirmations with simple organic framing; quote pages may use hands, flowers, butterflies, windows, or geometric motifs.
seasonal cues: Spring growth; summer freedom and connection; fall release and grounding; winter warmth and belonging.
forbidden: Tokenized diversity, exaggerated mixed features, stereotypes, crisis imagery, violence, drug use, visible injury, police scenes, weapons, or distress-centered compositions.
notes: The line should communicate that multiracial identity is ordinary, complex, and whole—not an aesthetic effect added to a generic character.
